div.head: Ps Cn for 31
div.ab: Nullus mediocris habebit nec custodiet canes, quos Angli greihounds appellant.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 625 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: No middling man shall have or keep the dogs which the English call greihounds (greyhounds).

note.seg: wie 26q adelsfreundlich, giebt Verf. Cnuts allgemeine Erlaubniss mit dem Rechte, Jaghunde zu halten, dem Adel allein
Favouring the nobility, as in 26 note q, the author gives Cnut's general permission, together with the right to keep hunting dogs, to the nobility alone

-nde in zwei Hss., ist später Singular mit stummem -e. Das Compositum ist Lehnwort vom Nord. greyhundr 'Hündin'; doch heisst auch grey allein dasselbe. Für Lyes grighund scheint einzige Quelle Wright-Wülker Vocab. 276, 3. Falsche Etymologie um 1310 s. o. S. 367*. Ass. de foresta Heinrichs II. 14 setzt dafür mastiui

-nde in two MSS is a later singular with mute -e. The compound is a loanword from Norse greyhundr 'bitch'; but grey alone also means the same. For Lye's grighund the only source seems to be Wright-Wülker, Vocab. 276, 3. False etymology around 1310, see above p. 367*. Henry II's Ass. de foresta 14 has mastiui instead
